review.summary:
The manuscript is a faithful, complete and readable account of archived run zt-thesis-plan (plan thesis@gpt-6.1-sol, archive commit 867fc9b). I re-derived the logic of P1–P7 myself rather than relying on the archived verdicts, and found no gap in the source argument. Every manuscript statement has the hypotheses, ranges, quantifiers, error terms and uniformity of its archived proposition. Where it differs, it states a form the archive actually proves and that is at least as strong: Proposition 5.1 with an absolute constant and x^{4/5}, and Lemma 4.2 for x ≥ 1. changes.md maps each result to its archived proofs and passing reviews. No mathematical correction was authorised in source/interventions.md and none was made. Every merged argument and editorial completion I checked holds.

The numerics are genuinely recomputed. reproduce.py checks the snapshot code against the SHA-256 hashes in accepted.json, reruns it, and evaluates the constants from their Euler products. I verified the data independently: a brute-force Python computation of V_f at x = 2.5·10^5 matches all 24 archived rows (relative error up to 8.5e-15). My own Euler products reproduce R_f, B_f, H_f(−1/2) and K_f to truncation level. My own Θ_f and F_f code reproduces Table 10.3 and every N_pred and deviation in Table 10.4. An independent least-squares fit reproduces C_data and C_prof in Table 10.5.

Citations match the supplied PDFs. The provenance section is accurate, and the PDF compiles cleanly and renders legibly.
review.statement_checks:
Theorem 1.1 against P7 and the plan: η_d = min{1/5, 1/(4d−1)}, 0 < ε < η_d/2, constants C(f,ε) and x_0(f,ε), uniformity in real x ≥ x_0 and real y ≥ 1 with f(y) ≤ x, and both bounds (1.8) and (1.9) are identical.

Constants:
- (1.6) defines R_f, B_f and K_f exactly as P6/P7 do.
- (1.10) agrees with P5 (29). Sympy confirms that (1−1/p)(α_p+β_p√p+δ_p p) equals the displayed local factor exactly, and that it equals (1−2/p²)(1−1/p)[a_p+(b_p−a_p)√p+(c_p−b_p)p].
- (1.11) is P5 (34).

Corollary 1.2: re-derived. With ε = δ the relative errors are (Y/x)^{1/8} ≤ x^{−δ/8} and x^{−δ/2}. The range is nonempty exactly when δ < η/3. The small-degree table (η = 1/5, 1/7, 1/11; ranges 13/15, 19/21, 31/33) is correct. The manuscript correctly says that the corollary is a plan consequence, not an approved proposition.

Chapters 3–8 against P1–P6:
- Prop 3.1: 3√x error and closed form, as in P1 (5) and (8).
- Prop 3.2: (d) holds for all R > 0 with 10/3 and 5/3, as P1 (20) and (22) prove.
- Prop 3.3: as in P1.
- Lemma 4.2: stated for x ≥ 1, valid via Prop 3.1. The constant in Prop 4.3 is 12·D·U·J·x^{3/2+ε}, which I checked.
- Prop 4.5: as in P2.
- Prop 5.1: K_c = 67 + 2·D_{1/10}, with the arithmetic checked.
- Prop 6.4: same 𝒜, constants and ranges as P4.
- Prop 7.2(a)–(f): as in P5.
- Prop 8.5 and Lemma 8.6: as in P6.

Corrected exposition of the source:
- Lemma 8.3: I checked the term-by-term bound (4+4d)p^{−3/2} for |z| ≤ p^{5/8}, the sum Σ ≤ 8(1+d), and the bound for the finitely many p ∈ 𝓑.
- Lemma 2.3(a): the Cauchy argument is fine.
- Prop 7.2(b): |α_p−1| ≤ 2p^{−2} is fine.

Residues and contour shift: q(1) = 1, q′(1) = −3/2, Res₀ = −2D_f(0)H = cH, and (s−1)s(s+1) = 3/8 at s = −1/2. The bound ζ(−1/2) ∈ [−1/4, −1/6] follows from (7.2), and the constants 195/512 and (32/3)·2^{−3/8} check out.

Exact cancellation: (9.1)/P7 (11) re-derived. The exponent bookkeeping (8d−3)/a = 2−1/a and (6d−5)/(2a) > 0 is correct, and so is every row of the error-budget table. Remark 1.3 is correctly hedged (fixed-ratio factor 1+O(r^{1/8})). Remark 1.4: V_f = V(x,Y) − E(x;1,1)² for f = t+1. Its local-factor identity checks out symbolically, and numerically K_{t+1} = 0.12847867 against c_2 = 0.12847867.
review.dependency_checks:
Each use of an earlier result meets that result's hypotheses:
- P2 uses only P1's density, closed form and l = 0 case (merged as Q(x;a,0), g(a,0)).
- P3 needs no dependency. The manuscript notes this and does not use the unneeded circle-method cutoff.
- P4 uses P1's second-moment identity, Ramanujan expansion and the tail and moment bounds 𝒯(R), 𝒩(R).
- P6 uses P5's factorisation, holomorphy, D_f(0) = −c/2 and residues.
- P7/Chapter 9 uses Prop 4.3 and Prop 4.5 with ε₁ = ε/2, Prop 5.1 (x^{4/5}, giving x^{9/5}·log 2x, which changes no final term), Prop 6.4 with R = Z^{1/d}, and Lemma 8.6 (which needs 2 ≤ Z ≤ Y ≤ x; x_0 guarantees Z ≥ max{2, f(1)} and R ≥ 2).
- The identification R̃_f = R_f (Prop 7.2(d)) is used before the logarithmic terms cancel, as in P7.
- The case Y < Z uses Prop 4.5 with z = y and |F_f(H)| ≤ (K_f + C)H^{−3/2}.

Merged arguments, all valid:
- Lemma 2.6 replaces P2's Σf′/f bound with P4's 2U·log(2x); only a constant changes.
- Lemma 2.5 proves multiplicativity via Dirichlet convolution.
- Lemma 2.7(d) uses C_ρ = max{d,|A_d|}; the dropped "1" is redundant since d ≥ 1.
- Lemma 6.2 matches P4 (16)–(18).
- Lemma 6.5's d = 1 and d ≥ 2 cases match P4 (31)–(32).

Archived reviews: all 14 are "pass" and the integration reports say composes = true (checked, not relied on). Appendix B's statements are accurate: approval of the first versions, and the Corollary deductions with ε = δ (Opus) and ε = δ/2 (Sol). I found no hidden assumption, sign error, range error or uniformity loss that would warrant a source-gap.
review.numerics_checks:
Computation path: reproduce.py hash-checks compute.py and counts.cpp against accepted.json and copies them into a temporary directory outside manuscript/. It runs compute.main() on the full grid and compares the results with the archived results.json: 270 rows, 0 mismatches, maximum relative difference 0. It then evaluates the constants from Euler products up to 10^7. The archived results are read only for that comparison, not copied into tables. reproduce.log (909 s run, 2026-11-06) agrees with reproduction.json. All 21 artifacts and the PDF match their hashes in build-inputs.json.

Independent checks (my own scripts in scratch_referee/):
1. Brute-force V_f(x,y) at x = 2.5·10^5 from a direct squarefree sieve and the closed-form g(q,l). All 24 archived rows for t²+1, t³+2 and 2t+1 match, with relative error at most 8.5e-15.
2. Euler products to 2·10^6 with ρ by brute force (p ≤ 200) and residue rules:
   - R_f: 0.392347679 / 0.395332424 / 0.378696892 / 0.420774325.
   - K_f: 0.13808263 / 0.13560752 / 0.14261331 / 0.12847867.
   - B_f and H_f(−1/2) agree with Table 10.1 to truncation level.
   - Vaughan c_2 from (1.2) is 0.12847868.
3. Θ_f remainders at H = 10²…10⁵ reproduce Table 10.3 to all six digits.
4. N_pred at x = 2.56·10^8 reproduces every entry and deviation of Table 10.4.
5. Unweighted OLS of C + a√r + br on the largest-x rows with r ≥ 0.01 (actual ratios) gives C_data = 0.134475 / 0.136321 / 0.141686 and C_prof = 0.134364 / 0.135793 / 0.141685, as in Table 10.5.

Other checks:
- Deviation-trend macros: 8 of 9 decreasing, exception at 0.005, sign change at 0.02, factor ≥ 18, 14.9%.
- Relative error sizes: x^{−1/11} ≈ 0.17 and x^{−1/7} ≈ 0.06.
- Truncation bound for K_f: |M_p−1| ≤ 9.1p^{−2} ≤ 10p^{−2}, 1.131, 3.6, hence 15p^{−2} and e^{15/N} − 1.
- The D_q local factors described in §10.1 are correct.
- Uncertainty labelling (heuristic envelope, OLS SEs, fixed-ratio SE of the mean) matches compute.py and reproduction.json.

Limitations:
- I did not rerun reproduce.py itself (about 15 minutes, several GB of memory). I relied on its shipped log and outputs plus the independent checks above.
- Floating-point rounding of the constants is not certified; the manuscript says so.
- Housekeeping only: the README quotes the runtime (914 s) of an earlier run than the shipped log (909 s). It labels this correctly and points to reproduction.json.
- A stray Claude Code `.claude/.cc-writes` directory sits under manuscript/generated. It is not a manuscript output.
review.citation_checks:
Checked against the supplied PDFs:
- BGPVW 1998, Lemma 2.2 and (2.6)–(2.7): Quoted Result 4.4 is verbatim in substance. The note about all residue classes versus Warlimont's coprime ones matches p. 6. The normalisation argument (E_2 = E) is valid.
- BGPVW Corollary 3: the singular series S_k(n) at k = 2 is the manuscript's 𝔖(n).
- Vaughan 2005:
  - The (1.13) Theorem at k = 2 matches (1.1).
  - (1.14)–(1.15) give c_2 = 8C_1(−ζ(−1/2))/(3ζ(2)²) and the stated local factor of C_1, with 3p³ = p^{2k−1} + 2p^{k+1}.
  - (1.5) recalls the BGPVW bound.
  - (1.10)–(1.11) give Warlimont's result for 1 ≤ Q ≤ x with F(y) ∼ c_2·y^{−3/2}, correctly attributed "according to that survey".
  - The remark that Croft's argument is faulty, and the x^{1+1/k} log x barrier, are accurate.
- Montgomery–Vaughan 2007, Corollaries 10.4 and 10.5 (pp. 329–330): match. The use with A = 2, −5/8 ≤ σ ≤ 1/4 and |t| ≥ 2 is within the hypotheses.
- Brüdern–Wooley 2011, the permitted post-2010 exception: the description of sparse moduli with weight f′(k), the Mikawa–Peneva upper bound, and the Goldston–Vaughan / Vaughan [10] approach via p₁ − p₂ = h·f(k) and the circle method matches its §1.
- Goldston–Vaughan 1997 and Vaughan 1998 I: title, venue and pages match the PDF headers and the Brüdern–Wooley reference list.

Bibliographic data checked against the reference lists of supplied papers:
- Croft 1975 and Warlimont 1980 (Vaughan 2005 refs).
- Montgomery 1970, Hooley 1975 I and Mikawa–Peneva 2005 (Brüdern–Wooley refs).

Unverifiable from supplied material, and disclosed in the README and changes.md:
- All DOIs, including Brüdern–Wooley's (from the plan) and BGPVW's (from the P2 proof). The supplied PDFs do not print them, except Vaughan 2005 and the Montgomery–Vaughan chapter DOI.
- Mirsky 1949, which comes only from the candidate list and is cited as background on the strength of its title. Appendix B's general disclaimer covers it.

Literature rules: all literature is pre-2011 apart from Brüdern–Wooley. No excluded author or paper is cited, and I opened no excluded source.
review.provenance_checks:
Appendix B against provenance.json:
- Archive commit 867fc9b…, harness commit 552a8f01…, and model-record revision fc217220…: all correct and correctly kept distinct.
- Selected plan thesis@gpt-6.1-sol and label zt-thesis-plan: correct.
- The eight role/model/CLI rows match exactly, and the table notes that CLI versions are not model-weight versions.
- Writer is claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Code 2.1.311); reviewers are claude-opus-5-5 and codex:gpt-6.1-sol. Both correct.
- The snapshot candidate label "codex-gpt-6.1-sol" and the acceptance wording "operator selected; not a proof of numerical correctness" match accepted.json.

Hint and reuse provenance matches source/interventions.md: the owner authorised the operator to read the thesis in order to write the hint, without stating any content, and the numerics were reused from the zt-neutral snapshot.

There is no human-authorship claim; the author line names the archived run.

Archived work is clearly separated from later additions: Remark 1.4, the K_f truncation bound, the consistency checks, the extrapolation decomposition and parts of reproduce.py are all marked as added in the write-up.

The intervention record authorises no mathematical correction, and changes.md correctly records none.

Exposure report: provenance.json and Appendix B contain the project GitLab URL (gitlab.com/mshepherd/…). Stating it is permitted; I did not open or fetch it. I did not read the excluded thesis, Dehnert 2015, other runs or other write-ups. I used only workspace files and supplied papers.
review.layout_checks:
How I checked: pdfinfo (47 A4 pages), full pdftotext -layout extraction, and pdftoppm renders of all pages. I inspected pp. 7–8 (theorem, corollary, exponent table, remarks), p. 35 (error-budget proof and table), pp. 40–42 (Table 10.4, Figures 10.1–10.2, Tables 10.5–10.6), p. 44 (Appendix Table A.3) and p. 47 (bibliography) visually.

Findings:
- No unresolved references or citations ("??") anywhere.
- main.log has no overfull or undefined warnings; only the harmless epstopdf shell-escape note.
- Cross-references print as Chapter / Appendix / Proposition with working hyperlinks, and the PDF bookmark for §9.3 is fixed.
- Equations are well typeset: (1.6)–(1.11), the multline (1.1), (9.2) and the residue computations.
- Tables use booktabs with digit grouping, and outward-rounded bounds are explained in the text.
- Both pgfplots figures are legible, with axis labels, legends and captions consistent with the data.
- The bibliography is complete: 12 entries, all cited, printed with DOI links.
- Notation is consistent after the revision-5 renames (C_ρ, ϑ_p, σ₀), and harness notes stay out of the mathematical text.

Cosmetic only, not requiring revision: each Appendix A table sits alone on a mostly empty float page (pp. 42–44).
